title: Sentence Completion
tagline: Year 2 — Using clue words, tone and logic to choose the right word for a blank

introduction.overview: A sentence-completion question has one or two blanks and four choices. The right choice makes the sentence logical, grammatical and consistent in tone. The sentence itself supplies clues: contrast words (but, although, despite, unlike), cause words (because, so, therefore), comparison words (like, as), and the general sense of the sentence. Finding the clue and the relationship it signals is the key skill.
introduction.placementRelevance: Sentence completion questions are commonly asked in the verbal ability section of company aptitude rounds, with single and double blanks.
introduction.realWorldContext: Choosing the right word in an email or report, so that a sentence says exactly what you intend, uses the same skill.

learningObjectives: Identify the clue word that signals contrast, cause or addition
Predict the missing word before looking at the options
Choose between words of similar form using sense and grammar
Solve double-blank sentences by testing pairs

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Contrast clues (but, although, despite, unlike, however) tell you the blank is opposite to a nearby idea. Cause clues (because, so, since) tell you the blank follows logically from another idea.

coreDefinitions: Clue: a word or phrase in the sentence that signals the meaning of the blank.
Contrast signal: although, but, despite, unlike, however, far from.
Cause/result signal: because, so … that, therefore, thus.
Double blank: two missing words that must work together.
Tone: the positive or negative feeling of a word.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The sentence almost writes the answer for you. If it says "Although the exam was difficult…", the next idea must run against "difficult", so a positive outcome (passed) fits. Predicting the word first protects you from attractive but wrong options.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Cover the options, read the sentence, and guess the missing word in your own words. Then look for the option closest to your guess and test it for grammar and tone.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Contrast
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Although / despite / but / unlike signals the opposite idea

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Cause
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Because / so … that / since signals a logical reason or result
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: So heavy that the match was postponed

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Comparison
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Like / as / than signals similarity or difference
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Unlike his talkative brother, Arun is quiet

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Paired words
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Not only … but also;  neither … nor;  either … or

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Double blanks
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Test each option pair in the sentence
importantRulesAndFormulas.simpleExample: Despite the heavy weather, the match continued

mainNarrative: Look for the clue. In "The rain was so heavy that the match had to be ___", the cause (heavy rain) points to the result: postponed. In "Although the exam was difficult, most students ___ it", although signals a contrast, so most students passed it.

In a double-blank sentence, test each pair. "Despite the ___ weather, the match ___ as scheduled" needs a contrast: heavy weather and continued. The pair pleasant … continued would not need "despite", and heavy … stopped would not contrast.
Comparison words help. "Unlike his ___ brother, Arun is quiet and reserved" needs the opposite of quiet: talkative.
Check grammatical fit. "Not only intelligent ___ hardworking" needs but also. "He neither smokes ___ drinks" needs nor. "The more he practised, ___ he became" needs the better.
Always reread the full sentence with your choice to check tone and sense. If the sentence sounds odd, try the next best option.

deepDiveAspects.title: Tone matching
deepDiveAspects.content: Positive and negative words must agree with the sentence. A sentence describing an angry response needs words like harsh or hostile, not gentle.

deepDiveAspects.title: Idiomatic pairs
deepDiveAspects.content: Some answers are decided by fixed pairs (not only … but also, neither … nor, hardly … when) rather than meaning alone.

solvedExamples.title: Contrast clue
solvedExamples.question: Although the exam was difficult, most students ___ it. (passed / feared / failed / skipped)
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: The result goes against the difficulty.

solvedExamples.title: Double blank
solvedExamples.question: Despite the ___ weather, the match ___ as scheduled.

steps.title: Signal
steps.explanation: Despite means the match went on although the weather was bad.

solvedExamples.title: Paired conjunction
solvedExamples.question: She is not only intelligent ___ hardworking.

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Find the clue, predict the word, match the closest option, and check grammar and tone.

commonMistakes.mistake: Choosing one word of a pair

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Eliminate options with the wrong tone first.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: Clue words appear in most sentences.
